primary_topics: Birthday toast for Charo Santos-Concio, June 14, 2008 -- congratulating her as the first woman to head a major network in the Philippines or elsewhere in the world

Three-part portrait: beauty (from the deepest recesses of her being); intelligence (not mere intellectuality but riveting and convincing); and leadership (not merely commanding but envisioning, inspiring, teaching, enabling)

The governing theological tribute: 'I do not merely say Congratulations. I say, The Lord has chosen you because He loves you. All your dreams and all your hopes are always fulfilled because He is always with you, beside you, above you, within you.'
The rhetorical method: 'To say that Charo is beautiful/intelligent/the boss is to say the truth. But not the whole truth.' -- the governing structure repeated three times
sub_topics: Beauty: 'does not come merely from the contours of her face or the sparkle of her eyes or the sweetness of her smile or the melody of her voice. It comes from the deepest recesses of her being, shining forth, glowing, radiating, penetrating and captivating. I do not merely behold her, I bathe in the glow of her sunshine; I drink of her like sweet wine and then relish the stupor of my merry drunkenness.'

Intelligence: 'mere intellectuality is barren, stale, unexciting, even boring. But Charo is riveting, tantalizing, enervating, uplifting. When she moves she projects, when she writes she persuades, when she whispers she entrals, when she speaks she convinces.'

Leadership: 'she does not merely command. She envisions, she inspires, she teaches, she leads. She does not merely do her job. She shows how it is done. She explains why it is done. She makes her people believe in themselves. She helps them overcome their puny limitations. She enables them to excel beyond themselves.'
First woman to head a major network: 'she is the first woman to head a major network whether here or elsewhere in this planet is to say the truth. But not the whole truth.'

The theological tribute: 'she does not need human exhortations to achieve her vision... What I wish for her is the Lord's benediction and sanctification. With humans, some things may not be possible. But with God, nothing is impossible.'; 'The Lord has chosen you because He loves you. All your dreams and all your hopes are always fulfilled because He is always with you, beside you, above you, within you, guiding you, blessing you, empowering you, sanctifying you, loving you, now and forever. Amen.'

stances.claim: The highest tribute CJP can offer Charo is not a professional compliment but a theological one: 'The Lord has chosen you because He loves you.' This moves the toast from the category of human congratulation to divine commissioning, reflecting CJP's belief that the most consequential validation comes not from peers but from God.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered June 14, 2008 as a birthday toast for Charo Santos-Concio -- congratulating her as the first woman to head a major television network in the Philippines or anywhere else in the world -- this address by CJP is structured around the repeated anaphora: 'To say that Charo is [beautiful / intelligent / the boss] is to say the truth. But not the whole truth.' Beauty: 'does not come merely from the contours of her face or the sparkle of her eyes... It comes from the deepest recesses of her being. I do not merely behold her, I bathe in the glow of her sunshine; I drink of her like sweet wine and then relish the stupor of my merry drunkenness.' Intelligence: 'mere intellectuality is barren, stale, unexciting, even boring. But Charo is riveting, tantalizing, enervating, uplifting. When she moves she projects, when she writes she persuades, when she whispers she entrals, when she speaks she convinces.' Leadership: 'she does not merely command. She envisions, she inspires, she teaches, she leads... She shows how it is done. She explains why it is done. She makes her people believe in themselves. She helps them overcome their puny limitations. She enables them to excel beyond themselves.' On being the first woman to head a major network: 'she does not need human exhortations to achieve her vision and accomplish her mission. What I wish for her goes beyond what is humanly possible. What I wish for her is the Lord's benediction and sanctification. With humans, some things may not be possible. But with God, nothing is impossible.' He closes with a theological blessing: 'The Lord has chosen you because He loves you. All your dreams and all your hopes are always fulfilled because He is always with you, beside you, above you, within you, guiding you, blessing you, empowering you, sanctifying you, loving you, now and forever. Amen.'
